﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾, meaning their Owner and the one who manages their affairs. He mentioned that He is the Lord of mankind, although He is Lord of all creation, for two reasons. The first: because mankind are the greatest of created beings, so by mentioning them He made known that He is their Lord, even though they are exalted. The second: because He commanded seeking refuge from their evil, so by mentioning them He made known that He is the One who grants refuge from them. He said "the King of mankind, the God of mankind" because among mankind there are kings whom it is claimed are their king, and among mankind there are those who worship other than Him; so He mentioned that He is their God and the One they worship, and that He is the One who must be sought for refuge and turned to, not the kings and the great.

He means: from the evil of the Whisperer (al-Shaytan). The meaning is: from the evil of the one who whispers (dhu al-waswas), so the modified noun is omitted. This is what al-Farra' said. The word (with a fatha on the waw), وَسْوَاس, is used as a noun meaning the one who whispers (al-muwaswis). The word (with a kasra on the waw), وِسْوَاس, is a verbal noun (masdar), meaning the whispering (al-waswasah). The same applies to الزَّلْزَال and الزِّلْزَال. Al-waswasah (whispering) is the inner speech of the soul. It is said: "His soul whispered to him a whispering (waswasah) and a whispering (wiswasah, with a kasra on the waw)." The word waswas is also used for the faint sound of a hunter and of dogs, and for the sound of ornaments. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"So he spent the night restless, kept awake by the dampness of the cold, the gusting of the wind from every direction, the whispering, and the rain showers."
[Shi'z: a man became anxious from illness or worry. Tha'd: dew, cold, and an ugly matter. Tadhawwub al-rih: the blowing of the wind from every direction, derived from the trickery of the wolf. Al-hidab (with a kasra on the ha'): rain showers.]

Al-A'sha said:

"You hear a whispering from the ornaments when she turns away, like the sound of a dry, rustling plant of 'ishriq that the wind has stirred."
[Al-'ishriq (on the pattern of zibrij): a plant that has leaves, and when it dries it flies away. Najd zajil: the wind made a sound in it.]

It is also said: the Whisperer, the Withdrawer (al-Khannas), is a son of Iblis. He brought him to Hawwa' (Eve), placed him before her, and said: "Look after him." Then Adam (peace be upon him) came and said: "What is this, O Hawwa'?" She said: "Our enemy brought this and said to me: 'Look after him.'" He said: "Did I not tell you not to obey him in anything? He is the one who deceived us until we fell into disobedience." Then he went to the child, cut him into four quarters, and hung each quarter on a tree, out of rage at him. Then Iblis came and said: "O Hawwa', where is my son?" She informed him of what Adam (peace be upon him) had done to him. He said: "O Khannas!" and the child came to life and answered him. He brought him back to Hawwa' and said: "Look after him." Then Adam (peace be upon him) came, burned him with fire, and scattered his ashes into the sea. Then Iblis (may he be cursed) came and said: "O Hawwa', where is my son?" She informed him of Adam's deed to him, so he went to the sea and said: "O Khannas!" and he came to life and answered him. He brought him back to Hawwa' a third time and said: "Look after him." Adam looked at him, slaughtered him, roasted him, and they both ate him together. Then Iblis came and asked her, and Hawwa' informed him. [Hawwa' is added from al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim.] He said: "O Khannas!" and he came to life and answered him, [and he came] from inside Adam and Hawwa'. Iblis said: "This is what I wanted. This is your dwelling in the chest of Adam's child. He grips the heart of the son of Adam as long as he is heedless and whispers. When he remembers God, he withdraws his heart and retreats." Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned this report in Nawadir al-Usul, with an isnad going back to Wahb ibn Munabbih. I do not think it is authentic, and God knows best.

He is described as al-Khannas because he hides a great deal. From this is the saying of God Most High: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede﴾ [al-Takwir: 15], meaning the stars, because they hide after appearing. It is also said: he is called that because he recedes when the servant mentions God, that is, he falls back. In a report: "Indeed, the Shaytan crouches upon the heart of the son of Adam. When he is heedless, he whispers; and when God is mentioned, he withdraws (khanasa), that is, he falls back and draws away."

Qatadah said: al-Khannas is the Shaytan, who has a snout like the snout of a dog in the chest of a human being. When a person is heedless, he whispers to him, and when the servant remembers his Lord, he withdraws. It is said: "I made him withdraw (khanastuhu), so he withdrew (khanasa)," that is, "I made him delay, so he delayed." Also, "akhnastuhu" has the same meaning. From this is the line of Abu al-'Ala' al-Hadrami, who recited to the Messenger of God (ﷺ):

"Even if they do mischief with evil, pardon them out of generosity; and if they withdraw from speech with you, do not ask."

Al-dahs means corruption. From Anas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the Shaytan places his snout upon the heart of the son of Adam. When God is mentioned, he withdraws; and when God is forgotten, he seizes the heart and whispers."

Ibn 'Abbas said: when the servant remembers God, [the Shaytan] withdraws from his heart and departs; when he is heedless, [the Shaytan] seizes his heart, speaks to him, and makes him wishful.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: the first thing the whispering appears in is the wudu' (ablution).

It is said: he was named al-Khannas because he returns when the servant is heedless of the remembrance of God. Al-khanas means returning. The rajaz poet said:

"And a companion who moves restlessly, increasing when you approach him with a hiss."
[Yamta'is: moves about.]

Ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the words of God Most High, ﴿the whisperer, the withdrawer﴾, two interpretations: the first is that he is the one who turns back from guidance through whispering. The second is that he is the one who departs from certainty through whispering.

Muqatil said: Indeed the Shaytan is in the form of a pig, and he runs through the son of Adam like the flow of blood in the veins; God has empowered him over that. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾.

In the Sahih (of al-Bukhari and Muslim) it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed the Shaytan runs through the son of Adam like the flow of blood." This confirms what Muqatil said.

Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, who said: "I asked God to show me the Shaytan and his place in the son of Adam, and I saw him: his hands were in his hands, his feet were in his feet, and his branches (mashā'ib) were in his body; except that he had a snout like the snout of a dog. When he remembers God, he shrinks back and bows his head, and when he is silent from the remembrance of God, he seizes the heart."

According to what Abu Tha'labah described, he is branched throughout the body, meaning that in every limb of it there is a branch of him. It is also narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, or another of the Successors (tabi'un), that he said, and he was then advanced in age: "I have not been safe from fornication, and nothing assures me that the Shaytan will not enter my penis and make it limp!" This saying shows you that he is branched throughout the body, and this is the meaning of Muqatil's words.

As for his whispering (waswasah): it is the calling to obedience to him by means of a hidden speech, whose meaning reaches the heart without hearing a sound.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 114, verse 6:

He informed that the whisperer may be from among mankind. Al-Hasan said: "They are two devils: the devil of the jinn whispers into the breasts of mankind, and the devil of mankind comes openly." Qatadah said: "Among the jinn there are devils, and among mankind there are devils, so seek refuge in Allah from the devils of mankind and jinn." It is related from Abu Dharr that he said to a man: "Have you sought refuge in Allah from the devils of mankind?" He said: "Are there devils among mankind?" He said: "Yes, due to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 112] ... the verse."

(Note: al-An'am 112 is the verse cited in the footnote of the original, and the translation above follows the text as given.)

Some scholars held that "mankind" here means the jinn. They were called "mankind" just as they were called "men" in His saying: ﴿And there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾ [al-Jinn: 6], and "a company" and "a group" (nafar), as in His saying: ﴿And when We turned towards you a group (nafar) of the jinn...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]. According to this, "and mankind" is an conjunction over "the jinn," and the repetition is due to the difference of the two wordings.

It is mentioned from some Arabs that he said while narrating: "A company of the jinn came and stood still. It was said: 'Who are you?' They said: 'People (nas) of the jinn.'" This is the meaning of the statement of al-Farra'.

It was also said: "al-waswas" is the devil itself. His saying "from the jinnah" explains that it is from the jinn, and "and mankind" is coordinated with "al-waswas." The meaning: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, from the evil of the whisperer, who is from the jinnah, and from the evil of mankind." According to this, he was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of mankind and jinn.

Al-jinnah is the plural of jinni, as it is said: insi and insiyy (human). The ha' is for the feminine form of the collective noun.

It was also said: Iblis whispers into the breasts of the jinn just as he whispers into the breasts of mankind. According to this, "in the breasts of mankind" is general to all. And "from the jinnah and mankind" is an explanation of what whispers in his breast.

It was also said: the meaning of "from the evil of the whisperer" is the whispering that comes from the jinnah and mankind, and it is the speech of the soul (hadith al-nafs).

It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: [Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has overlooked for my community what their souls speak of, as long as they do not act upon it or speak it.] Narrated by Abu Hurairah, recorded by Muslim.

And Allah, Exalted is He, knows best what is meant by that.
